Sureshwar Thakur, J. (Oral)
1.
In the amended writ petition, the present petitioner land loser has claimed two reliefs.

The first relief relates to the making of a lapsing declaration under Section 24 (2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (herein after referred to as ' the Act of 2013').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The relief (supra) becomes abandoned by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. The second relief is for the subject acquisition becoming released.
The said ground is based upon release order (Annexure P-6) and on the report of the Joint Site Inspection Committee appended with the amended writ petition as Annexure P-7.
A reading of the said Annexures does bring-forth ex facie facts, which support the writ prayer from releasing the subject acquisitions.

The reason becomes embodied to the factum, that the subject acquisitions are located in Atam Nagar colony,
and, in the table appended with Annexure P-6, it has been detailed that the said subject colony,
wherein, the subject land exist, thus has been regularised.

Therefore, 1 of 2 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086497-DB there was no occasion for the making of an award in respect of such Narinder Kumar vs State Of Haryana And Ors on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27860953/

sentences.text: Resultantly, the launching of acquisition proceedings have to be quashed.
Moreover, the making of the apposite award also deserves to become quashed and set aside.
3. After allowing the writ petition, the subject acquisitions are in terms of Annexure P-6 accordingly released from the acquisitions.
If the acquiring authority is retaining possession over the subject acquisitions, thereupon it is directed to forthwith retrieve possession thereof to the present petitioner.

Moreover, if certain revenue entries, thus declaring the acquiring authority to be the owner of the subject acquisitions, hence exist in the relevant record, thereupon, the said revenue entries be asked to be deleted from the relevant revenue records.

4. It is further clarified that in case the present petitioner has received compensation, as determined under the award concerned, thereupon, he shall forthwith return the said received compensation by him, thus to the acquiring authority.

However, in case the compensation determined under the award concerned is not released to the present petitioner, thereupon the acquiring authority is directed to forthwith appropriate it in the appropriate head of accounts.
5. In view of the above, the present petition stands disposed of.
(SURESHWAR THAKUR)
JUDGE 11.07.2024 (SUDEEPTI SHARMA)
